title: Teluni Catalog and Composition Design
heading: Policy inputs
text:
Policy inputs
The design applies these policies without changing them:
**Catalogs are configurable.** They are tenant-owned, user-configurable collections with typed fields and records. Products, menus and weekly agendas are configurations, not mandatory schemas ([configurable catalogs](release-policies.md#configurable-catalogs)).
**Customization stays inside safe types.**
Field types cover text, numbers, booleans, dates and times, selections, money, authorized media and scoped record references.
Customization never runs code, SQL or markup.
Stable field identity preserves bindings, and renaming a label never changes meaning.
A destructive change needs explicit handling.
Published versions keep their own schema and values.
**Money is exact and per branch.** Every amount has an explicit currency and exact representation, with no conversion. A company base price may be overridden per branch, and the effective branch value is previewed.
**Promotions and availability.** A promotion applies only within its validity, then falls back to the normal price. Competing promotions for the same product and branch are rejected. Unavailable items are hidden by default, unless a view chooses to show them as unavailable. All of this must be evaluable offline.
**Catalog views never hide text silently.** Views bind fields into lists, tables, menus or agendas, with automatic or manual pagination, grouping, and a minimum readable text size. Names and prices are never silently clipped; an overflow that cannot be resolved is a visible validation error.
**Freeform composition** ([composition and regional playback](release-policies.md#composition-and-regional-playback)):
Areas can be positioned and resized freely.
Layouts are versioned text that can be copied, imported and exported.
Areas advance independently, with optional coordinated pages.
Each area has its own schedules and an optional default. A regional schedule survives page changes; when it ends, the area returns to the page, then to its default, then to neutral output.
Page durations never cut a full video.
Several videos can play at once on a measured profile.
New areas start muted, and audio is mixed only deliberately.
Area failures stay isolated.
**Price saves publish.** An authorized price save automatically publishes the affected published content as a new version and never publishes unrelated drafts.
The save is accepted only if every affected target is authorized; otherwise the whole save is rejected, with no partial distribution.
Saved, queued, failed and published states are distinguished.
Duplicates and stale work never replay an older price.
A publication holds consistent layout, schema, record, price and media versions ([assignment and publication](release-policies.md#assignment-and-publication), [publication impact](identity-and-access.md#publication-impact-and-delayed-work)).
**Permissions** follow the [matrix](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix): "Author layouts, playlists and agendas", "Change prices with automatic publication", "Create shared company catalog/schema", and "Edit records without automatic publication". Anyone who may distribute prices automatically needs strong authentication.

title: Teluni Catalog and Composition Design
heading: Concepts
text:
Concepts
A **catalog** is a named collection owned by the company or by one branch, with a **schema**: an ordered list of **fields**. Each field has a stable identifier, a label that may change, a type that never changes, whether it is required, and type options. Every schema change increments the catalog's schema version.
A **record** is one entry of a catalog. It has a value for each field, an availability flag, and a position. Records of money fields are the **prices**.
A **price** is the base amount of a money field on a record. A **branch override** replaces it for one branch. A **promotion** replaces it within a local validity window, for the whole company or for one branch.
A **layout** is a reusable canvas (landscape 1920×1080 or portrait 1080×1920 units) with **areas**. Each area has a rectangle, a stacking order, a background, audio settings and a kind:
**Media** areas play playlists.
**Catalog** areas show a **catalog view**, which binds catalog fields into a list, table, menu or agenda with pagination and grouping.
A **program with a layout** has one output per area, instead of the single `screen` output. Each output has schedule rules and a default, exactly as programming defines them.
**Pages** optionally coordinate some areas: a layout may define pages with durations. Page-controlled areas change content together at each page boundary, while independent areas keep their own timing.

title: Teluni Catalog and Composition Design
heading: Catalogs
text:
Catalogs
**Ownership and visibility** mirror playlists:
A catalog belongs to the company or to one branch.
A company catalog is visible to anyone with `catalogs.view` anywhere in the company, and its schema is editable only with company-wide `catalogs.manage`.
A branch catalog needs the capability on its branch.
A program may use a catalog only when every branch the program reaches is inside the catalog's scope, as programming requires for playlists.
**Field types**, with their stored and published values:

A required field must have a value on every record. Text values are trimmed, and empty text counts as absent. A schema allows at most 60 fields, archived ones included. Money fields are never required, because prices are saved apart from other values by people who may edit prices.
**Schema changes** are saved as the whole ordered field list with the expected catalog version, like rules.
New fields get identifiers.
A field's type, currency, decimal places and reference target never change. To change one, a person adds a new field and archives the old one.
Leaving a field out of the list deletes it only while no record, branch price or promotion holds a value for it; otherwise the save is refused with the count, and the field must be archived.
Labels are unique among active fields, ignoring case. Shortening a text field's maximum length or narrowing a number's range is refused while stored values would break it, with their count.
A reference field's target must be an active catalog whose scope covers the field's catalog: a company catalog for any catalog, or a catalog of the same branch.
Archiving a field keeps its values and hides it from editing and new bindings. Published versions keep their own schema copy.
A field bound by a layout draft cannot be archived until the binding is removed; the error names the layouts.
Making a field required is refused while any record lacks a value for it, and the error says how many records lack one.
Selection options keep their identifiers. A removed option is refused while records use it.
**Records** are saved one at a time with the record's expected version.
A record's values are a map from field identifier to value, validated against the current schema.
Unknown and archived field identifiers are refused.
References must point to an existing record of the target catalog that the caller may see.
Records are listed in their stored order, with a cursor. Moving a record after another one, or to the top, is its own versioned operation.
A record's title is the value of the catalog's first active text field; lists and references show it.
A record whose identifier another record references cannot be deleted (`CATALOG_RECORD_REFERENCED`); the error counts the referring records.
Availability is a built-in flag, not a field. A view hides unavailable records unless it shows them as unavailable.
A catalog holds at most 5,000 records, and a record's values at most 16 KiB of JSON.
**Prices.** A money value on the record is the **base price**. Overrides and promotions are separate rows, so each change is attributable and checked on its own. The base price and each branch override are saved one at a time with the record's version, which every price save increments:
**Branch overrides** set an amount for one branch of the catalog's scope. They are possible only on company catalogs, because a branch catalog already has one branch.
**Promotions** set an amount for a local window `[start, end)` (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, evaluated in each screen's local time like schedules), for the whole scope or for one branch.
Two promotions of the same record and field are refused when their windows overlap and their branch scopes intersect. A company-wide promotion intersects every branch.
Promotions are never edited: a person removes one and adds another. They do not change the record's version.
**Effective price** for a branch at a local instant: an applicable promotion, otherwise the branch override, otherwise the base price. When a record has no base price and no override for the branch, the price is absent, and a view shows the field as empty.
Every price change (base, override or promotion) is a **price save** under the access policies: it needs `prices.edit` on the scope it affects and strong authentication. Increment 4 adds automatic publication. Until then, price saves are drafts like any other edit, because no published content binds catalogs yet.

title: Teluni Catalog and Composition Design
heading: Layouts
text:
Layouts
**Layouts** are owned like catalogs and playlists, and authored with `programming.edit`, because the matrix groups layouts with playlists and agendas. A layout has:
a name;
an orientation;
1–12 areas;
0 or 2–20 pages;
a version and a schema version.
**Areas:**
**Geometry.** Integer canvas units with `x ≥ 0`, `y ≥ 0`, `width ≥ 40`, `height ≥ 40`, inside the canvas, and a unique stacking order. Overlap is allowed (for example, a logo over a video) and drawn by stacking order.
**Appearance.** A background color in `#RRGGBB`, and a fit for media: `contain` by default, or `cover`, which crops but never distorts.
**Audio.** Muted by default, with volume 0–100. Mixing two audible areas needs an explicit confirmation flag on the layout.
**Kind.**
A **media** area plays playlists that its program output selects.
A **catalog** area shows a catalog view.
**Catalog views:**
**Data.** A catalog, and the bound fields in order. Each bound field has a role: `title`, `subtitle`, `price`, `image`, `detail` or `group`.
**Presentation.** `list`, `table`, `menu` (title and price aligned) or `agenda` (grouped by `weekdays`, then sorted by `time` fields).
**Text.** A text size in canvas units (the minimum readable size is 24 units, about 2.2% of 1080). Text never shrinks below it.
**Unavailable records.** Hidden, or shown as unavailable.
**Grouping.** By a `selection` field, in option order.
**Pagination.** Automatic every 5–120 seconds (10 by default), or by page when the area is page-controlled.
**Overflow is validated.** The layout check computes how many records fit per page from the area's height, the text size and the fields shown. A title or price that does not fit its column at the chosen size fails validation and names the record. Records are never clipped or truncated, and a view with too many records only gains pages.
**Pages and coordination:**
A layout with pages has explicit page durations (1–600 seconds).
When the page-controlled media areas use a playlist, the check suggests a duration that covers its longest video, and rejects a duration shorter than any video those areas play on that page.
A page-controlled media area names, for each page, one media item from the layout's scope. A shorter video holds its last frame.
A page-controlled catalog area names the view page or the group to show: a `selection` choice, or an agenda's ISO weekday (`"1"` for Monday to `"7"`).
Independent areas ignore pages.
A regional schedule on a page-controlled area overrides that area only while it lasts; the area then returns to the current page.
**Text representation:** a layout exports as versioned JSON (`teluni.layout`, schema 1) with areas, views, pages and bindings by stable identifier. Importing validates it like any save, inside the importer's scope. References to catalogs, fields or media that the importer cannot see are reported and must be remapped, never silently kept.

title: Teluni Catalog and Composition Design
heading: Programs with layouts
text:
Programs with layouts
**Choosing a layout.** A program chooses either no layout, which keeps the single `screen` output, or one layout. Choosing a layout is a versioned program change.
**Outputs.**
Each area becomes an output keyed by the area's stable key, with the existing rule and default model.
A media area output selects playlists.
A catalog area output may select playlists for its regional schedules, and its default is the area's view.
**Changing the layout.**
Outputs of areas that no longer exist are removed only when the layout change is confirmed.
The response lists rules that would be lost, and the panel asks for confirmation.
**Scope.** The program's reach must fit inside the scopes of the layout and of every catalog its views use, as playlists do.
**Evaluation.** The evaluator is unchanged and runs per output. Coordinated pages are a pure function of the page durations and a cycle anchored at local midnight. Every screen of a group therefore shows the same page at the same local time, and the preview can show it.

title: Teluni Catalog and Composition Design
heading: Publication protocol 2
text:
Publication protocol 2
A program without a layout keeps publishing protocol 1, byte for byte, so current screens are unaffected. A program with a layout publishes **protocol 2**, which adds the following to the manifest:
**`layout`.** The canvas, the areas (geometry, stacking order, appearance, audio, kind), the catalog views and the pages, copied from the layout's draft at publication.
**`outputs` per area.** Rules and defaults, with the catalog-view default marked as `{"view": true}`.
**`catalogs`.** For each catalog a view uses:
a schema snapshot with only the bound fields;
every record with its values, availability and position;
each money field's base price, branch overrides and promotions limited to the branches the program reaches;
media referenced by `media` fields, in the publication's media list.
A screen receives the program's single manifest. To resolve overrides and promotions for its branch, it needs its `branchId`, which the sync response gains next to `rotation`. Effective prices, availability, pagination and pages are evaluated on the screen from the snapshot, trusted time and zone offsets, with fixtures shared by the API's preview and the player, like schedules.
Protocol negotiation is unchanged. A screen that supports only protocol 1 and desires a protocol 2 publication reports `INCOMPATIBLE` and keeps its active generation, and the panel shows why.

title: Teluni Catalog and Composition Design
heading: Automatic price publication
text:
Automatic price publication
A price save on a record of catalog C:
**Authorizes the save.** Base, override or promotion scope, with strong authentication.
**Finds the affected targets.** These are the programs whose latest publication includes C. The publication's catalog rows are indexed for this lookup.
**Authorizes every target.** The saver must hold `publications.publish` on each one. If any is outside their scope, the whole save is refused with `PRICE_TARGET_FORBIDDEN`, and nothing is saved or distributed.
**Commits the price and one durable intent per affected program** in the same transaction. Each intent holds the program, the price change's sequence number and the author.
A processor in the API (leased rows, like the mail outbox of ADR-0026) turns each intent into a new generation:
It copies the program's latest publication content.
It replaces only that catalog's price rows with the current prices: base, overrides and promotions.
It publishes through the normal path with `restoredFromGeneration` null and `trigger: "price"`.
It never takes drafts of rules, playlists, layouts or other records.
Intents are coalesced per program, so the newest price wins and an older intent never overwrites a newer generation. Each intent is processed at most once per program and price sequence, so a retry is safe. Failures retry with back-off and stay visible as `failed` with the reason.
The panel shows each price save as saved, queued, published or failed per program. A revoked author blocks intents not yet processed, as the access policies require.

title: Teluni Catalog and Composition Design
heading: Abuse limits
text:
Abuse limits
Per company: 200 catalogs and 500 layouts. Per catalog: 60 fields and 5,000 records. Per selection field: 100 options. Per record and money field: 100 promotions. Per layout: 12 areas, 20 pages and 6 catalog views. Exceeding a limit answers `CATALOG_LIMIT_REACHED` or `PROGRAMMING_LIMIT_REACHED`, naming the limit. Record values are bounded by type and by 16 KiB per record.

title: Teluni Catalog and Composition Design
heading: Decisions
text:
Decisions
The agent took these decisions on 2026-10-20 under the owner's delegation:
**Catalog model.** Company or branch ownership like playlists, and schemas of typed fields with stable identifiers and immutable types. Changes are whole-schema saves with versions, with archiving instead of destructive deletion. Availability is a built-in flag.
**Field types.** `text`, `longText`, `number` (canonical decimal strings), `boolean`, `date`, `time`, `weekdays`, `selection`, `money`, `media` and `reference`, with the bounds above. No formula, code or markup type.
**Money (ADR-0032).** Integer minor units with one ISO 4217 currency per field, no conversion, and display formatting by locale only. Every money field is a designated price.
**Prices.** Base price on the record, branch overrides and promotions as separate rows. Promotions use local windows evaluated per screen. Overlapping promotions with intersecting branch scopes are refused. The effective price is promotion, then override, then base.
**Permissions.** `catalogs.view`, `catalogs.edit`, `catalogs.manage` and `prices.edit` as in the table, with prices always under strong authentication. Layouts use `programming.edit`.
**Layouts.** Up to 12 freeform areas on a fixed canvas per orientation, with media and catalog areas, catalog views with roles, presentation, grouping and timed pagination, and overflow validated, never clipped. Muted by default, with mixed audio only after explicit confirmation. Versioned JSON import and export.
**Programs with layouts.** Areas become program outputs with the existing rules and evaluator. Catalog areas default to their view. Pages are a deterministic cycle anchored at local midnight.
**Protocol 2.** Added only for programs with a layout, carrying a layout copy, bound-field schema snapshots, records, prices, overrides and promotions for the branches reached, and the screen's `branchId` in the sync response. Protocol 1 stays unchanged for programs without a layout.
**Automatic price publication.** All-target authorization before commit, durable coalesced intents in PostgreSQL processed by a leased in-API worker, and new generations that change only the catalog's prices of the latest publication.

title: Teluni Catalog and Composition Design
heading: Alternatives considered
text:
Alternatives considered
**A fixed product schema with optional extra fields.** Simpler queries, but it imposes product semantics on agendas and other catalogs, which the owner rejected (P05).
**One JSON document per catalog.** Fewer tables, but every record edit would rewrite the document, concurrent editors would conflict constantly, and references and prices could not be checked or audited per row.
**Decimal numbers or floats for money.** A float cannot represent cents exactly. A decimal type without a currency invites mixing currencies. Integer minor units with a currency per field are exact, simple to compare and portable to the player (ADR-0032).
**Republishing every affected program from its current drafts on a price save.** Would ship unrelated drafts, which the policies forbid. Only the price rows change in the new generation.
**Live catalog reads by screens.** Would make playback depend on the server and mix revisions; the publication snapshot keeps prices and layout consistent offline (ADR-0023).
**A layout engine with free HTML or SVG.** Flexible, but executable markup is forbidden and its rendering cannot be validated for overflow or reproduced natively. Typed areas and views are validated data.

Its original combined scope is explicitly split: **PH-18** retains customer acceptance, measured cost/support, actual support coverage and capacity-qualified offer evidence; **PH-19** retains billing-issuer/fiscal-process readiness. Neither is completed or waived. PJ-14 must collect pilot results and PJ-27 must implement/qualify the selected commercial controls before their use. This preserves the original evidence obligations without asking the owner to approve the same policy again.
**Price validation:** BRL 79.90/company/month for up to two screen licenses; BRL 29.90/month for each additional license. These are owner-approved initial validation prices, not a published offer, proven willingness to pay, profitability result or delivered entitlement. Initially offer one monthly plan in Brazil/BRL with the approved delivered product capabilities; no permanent free plan, annual offer or financial referral incentive. Public signup still requires all applicable readiness gates. No subscription, quota, payment, tax, billing issuer or commercial lifecycle implementation exists today. No paid service, customer contact, invoice, contract or public launch is authorized by this document.

title: Teluni Initial Commercial Policies
heading: Pilot and public trial
text:
Pilot and public trial
The first candidate pilot may receive **30 free software days for up to two screens**, starting only after functional setup and the operator's explicit start confirmation. Hardware, travel, installation beyond the included onboarding and content-production services are separate. Confirm participation/physical devices under PH-08, written/comparably attributable commercial agreement under PH-18 and privacy/readiness before real use. Owner approval is not customer acceptance. Extensions must be bounded, justified and recorded.
Present intended post-pilot price/conditions before starting. Conversion requires explicit commercial acceptance and the first confirmed payment; no unexpected automatic charging, silent lifetime discount or indefinite free continuation. Collect core usability, offline/recovery and device results alongside physical storage, transfer/processing, onboarding/support time, customer objections and willingness to continue. Public use of the client's name, logo, images or testimonial needs separate permission.
Public eligible verified companies receive an automatically activated **14-day trial**, starting at company activation, with a visible end instant and notices. No card is required and there is no permanent free subscription. The trial includes up to **two screens, one branch, five members and 2 GiB of original media**, plus **10 GiB of player media transfers** during the trial. Scope/abuse checks and qualified global capacity are admission prerequisites; do not substitute routine manual company approval for the PH-11 signup decision. Publish only an offer the host can actually admit safely.
At trial end, disallow new publishing, uploads and device enrollment. An authenticated, otherwise-authorized account may retain explicitly permitted contracting, account recovery and export paths in a **commercially restricted** state. This is distinct from a security-suspended account/company: commercial exceptions cannot bypass identity or security suspension. One evaluation per legitimate organization, with attributable assisted exceptions and proportionate abuse controls; email-domain/IP/name similarity alone neither proves shared ownership nor merges companies. No automatic trial extension; a justified exception must be bounded/audited.

title: Teluni Initial Commercial Policies
heading: Screen licenses and pricing
text:
Screen licenses and pricing
One screen license authorizes one player/device for one independently programmed playback output. Multiple regions, images/videos, catalog views or simultaneous functions within that output do not incur separate screen fees. The application does not claim to detect the number of physical panels attached through HDMI cloning. Multiple independent outputs need their own supported profile and explicit licensing before sale.
Customers contract a fixed license capacity per billing period. Assignment occupies a license until explicitly deallocated; connectivity/heartbeat does not create, cancel or meter the subscription. Turning off a TV does not reduce the contracted package. Separate companies do not silently share a minimum fee or discounts.
For the initial validation offer, one or two screens cost the BRL 79.90 company minimum. For `n > 2`, the proposed monthly total is BRL 79.90 + BRL 29.90 × (`n` − 2). Example totals: three screens BRL 109.80, four BRL 139.70 and ten BRL 319.10. Automatic table-based offers stop at ten licenses initially; larger fleets need a capacity/cost-qualified quote, without an automatic volume discount. Ten is an offer boundary, not a platform architecture limit; the reference 100-player benchmark is not measured host capacity.
Replace a failed player through an explicit license transfer and revocation, without an extra replacement charge. An unreachable old player may retain its already-issued authorization until expiry, at most seven days. Allow one pending replacement per license, report any overlap and prevent repeated replacement rotation; this is an explicit recovery exception, not an unlimited extra license. Cross-company reassignment still needs verified wipe/reset under the release security policy.
The single initial plan includes the approved capabilities that have actually been delivered. Never sell roadmap features as available. Do not gate HTTPS, isolation, required MFA, recovery, security fixes or reliable offline operation as paid upgrades. Do not separately charge per member/branch or per simultaneous screen function initially; explicit qualified technical limits still apply to members, branches, records, fields, layouts and imports. "No per-user fee" does not mean infinite resources. Trial-specific limits remain distinct.

title: Teluni Initial Commercial Policies
heading: Hardware, onboarding and support
text:
Hardware, onboarding and support
Customers initially supply compatible displays/players, power and network. Teluni must qualify the devices it advertises under PH-08 and diagnose its software faults; do not promise all Smart TVs are supported. Hardware resale/lease is not selected.
Include one remote onboarding/training session up to **60 minutes**. Quote onsite work, travel, physical installation, network/electrical services and extraordinary setup separately before acceptance; any first-pilot concession must be explicit. Include delivered tools/templates and usage guidance, not recurring artwork, catalog entry, campaign production or outsourced daily content operation. Paid AI and unlimited human work are not included by implication. Record the cost of included onboarding too.
P23/P24 were conditional recommendations. **Email/form are the baseline record channels; WhatsApp is optional only after actual coverage is confirmed.** No phone number/address/account is invented. Actual operator availability, support window and calendar remain **unknown under PH-18**, rather than asserting a 09:00–18:00 or 24/7 commitment. Use explicitly arranged pilot support while coverage is being established; before any public support offer, publish only the verified window and confront it with restaurant evening/weekend needs.
The selected target is a **useful first response within one business day of the established coverage calendar**, not an automated receipt or fixed resolution deadline. It cannot be advertised as an unconditional service commitment before that coverage is verified. Prioritize critical incidents and communicate according to real coverage; no formal availability/resolution SLA is sold at this stage. Repeated support demand calls for product improvements, training or offer review, not an arbitrary bug-support cutoff. Content access continues to require PH-11 scoped consent, expiry and the support person's real identity.
Explain residential power/network limitations, maintenance and incident communication before the pilot. Normal playback can continue from a valid local generation, but login, publishing, recovery and current diagnostics still depend on services/network. Formal SLA offers require measured compatible infrastructure and support; internal targets are not a commercial guarantee.

title: Teluni Initial Commercial Policies
heading: Payment, expiry, cancellation and retention
text:
Payment, expiry, cancellation and retention
Start with **monthly prepayment**, explicit billing dates/license quantity and **Pix/bank transfer with attributable manual reconciliation**. A screenshot alone does not prove settled payment. Only an explicitly authorized platform billing operator may confirm settlement or change commercial grants; company administrators may request/manage their own contracted capacity/cancellation without marking themselves paid. Concrete capabilities remain D-12 review, not implemented role identifiers. No bank destination, payment-provider integration, tax treatment or fiscal issuer is selected here. PH-19 must establish the appropriate billing/fiscal process before charging. Gateway/card automation remains future; basic commercial authorization cannot be deferred just because invoicing is manual.
Late-payment policy: notices and **seven days of commercial grace after the due date**. Thereafter deny new publications/enrollment and new commercial playback renewals, while allowing only explicitly authorized regularization/recovery/export paths for otherwise valid accounts. Maintain the security-suspension distinction. Do not invent penalties/interest or silent billable continuation; final conditions require review before contracting.
For trial, paid-period expiry/cancellation and applicable grace, future player authorization must be bounded by **both** the known commercial playback deadline and the maximum seven-day offline renewal interval. The shorter bound wins. Do not retroactively claim that an unreachable device received a newly shortened deadline, instantly stopped or erased its cache. Existing valid leases may survive an unreachable revocation until their previously issued deadline. On reconnect, reconcile current payment/authorization and content validity; no reset of an expired commercial period or bypass through old snapshots. These are required behaviors to qualify, not an implemented credential format.
Offer simple monthly cancellation without a minimum-stay penalty for future renewals; normally retain the already-paid period to its end, subject to legitimate security controls. Show the effective date/license impact and export path. Refunds, exceptions and applicable rights belong to transparent reviewed terms, not a fabricated legal conclusion or waiver. No annual prepayment/discount is offered initially. Do not silently stack pilot, volume or referral discounts.
Select a **30-day product window for authorized reactivation/export** after commercial end, without edit/publication. This is not a promise to erase every byte on day 31. Reconcile PH-13 personal-data/audit/backup obligations, the at-least-90-day publication-history target and protected active/staging/recovery references. Distinguish limited account access, physical deletion and offline cache erasure. Measure the cost of closed-trial retention and stop new admission when safe capacity is unavailable.

title: Teluni Initial Commercial Policies
heading: Economics, market and readiness
text:
Economics, market and readiness
Initial market is **Brazil/BRL**, with internationalization retained and no silent currency conversion. Foreign sales, annual plans, automated billing, recurring commissions and financial referral rewards require later evaluation. Record partner interest without a current incentive; referrals grant no access to customer data or shared human credentials.
No new recurring procurement is authorized now. With received revenue or a demonstrated operating need, prepare a total-cost budget and a separately approved procurement/migration proposal. Residential hosting, backup, identity and reliable email requirements are not waived by zero procurement budget; unresolved readiness prevents operation/admission. Revenue alone neither proves capacity nor authorizes spending.
Use an **at least 70% steady-state contribution-margin target** as an owner-approved validation goal. For this exercise, deduct applicable taxes/fees and attributable variable costs including valued recurring support; keep onboarding, fixed costs and investment recovery separately visible and do not double-count them. Value the owner's time initially at **BRL 50/hour as a stated analytical assumption**, not measured salary or an external-service price. Fixed costs belong in break-even analysis; cash increment, economic allocation and sunk investment are distinct.
At BRL 79.90 and a 70% target, the deductible-cost budget would be BRL 23.97/month/company. This is arithmetic, not a measured cost or proven profit. The pilot must determine whether actual taxes, transfer/processing, support and other attributable costs fit; revise price/offer before expanding if they do not. Unknown taxes or own labor are never zero by default. Qualified fiscal/legal review precedes charging/public terms; source Apache-2.0 licensing does not replace SaaS terms or fiscal documentation.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Status and scope
text:
Status and scope
**Approved detailed design for the server side of D-03, 2026-10-19.** The owner approved all nine [decisions for review](#decisions-for-review) as proposed under [PH-22](human-actions.md#ph-22), including ADR-0027, and asked for implementation in [PJ-08](implementation-plan.md#current-work). Approval authorizes implementation in local and CI environments with simulated players; [implementation status](#implementation-status) records what exists.
In scope: the device identity and its company/branch assignment, temporary-code enrollment, the device credential and how the API authenticates it, reported capabilities and the configured rotation (FR-03), the server's offline authorization deadline (AT-15), renaming, moving between branches, unlinking, erasure confirmation and reassignment (FR-02, P24), permissions, abuse limits, audit, data, contracts, panel workflow and verification.
Out of scope, with their owners: the Android application and its secure local storage, clock estimation and enforcement of the deadline on the device (D-07, PJ-12); signed authorization envelopes, manifests and synchronization (D-04, PJ-11); content assignment to devices and groups (PJ-10); trial, license and quota admission for enrollment (PJ-27); qualifying any hardware or orientation profile (PH-08). The design leaves explicit hooks for each and claims none of them.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Policy inputs
text:
Policy inputs
The design applies these selected policies without changing them:
Pairing codes are temporary, single-use, bound to the requesting device, rate-limited and safe under concurrent claims; the claiming person must already be authorized for the destination company and branch; a displayed code is not an enduring credential ([security requirements](security-and-i18n.md#pairing-and-device-lifecycle), FR-02).
Pairing, moving, unlinking and resetting devices is company-wide for administrators and limited to authorized source and destination branches for branch managers; operators need an additional grant ([permission matrix](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix)). Administrator and branch-manager grants count only in strongly authenticated sessions (P12).
Offline authorization expires no later than seven days after its last successful online renewal (AT-15, P22); commercial deadlines may shorten it (PJ-27).
Unlink needs explicit authorized confirmation, server revocation and a distinct pending-erasure state; private content, configuration and credentials are cleared on reconnection; reassignment to another company requires verified cleanup or a controlled reset; revoked access, unreachable device and confirmed erasure stay distinct (P24).
Player identities are separate from human identities and restricted to their own assignment, media and reports. Raw codes, credentials and credential-bearing links never reach logs, errors, screenshots or support bundles. No custom cryptography or token scheme.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Mechanism overview
text:
Mechanism overview
The flow follows the shape of the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant ([RFC 8628](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628)): a device without a keyboard shows a short code, and a person who is already signed in elsewhere enters it. Teluni does not route devices through Keycloak, because devices are not human principals and Keycloak holds only human identities (ADR-0024); the API module plays both the authorization-server and resource-server role for devices.
Player                                API (devices module)                    Panel (signed-in person)
  │ generate 256-bit credential C            │                                      │
  │ POST /device-enrollments              │                                      │
  │   { credentialHash: SHA-256(C), report } │                                      │
  │ ◀── { enrollmentId, userCode, expiresAt, pollInterval }                         │
  │ show userCode on screen                  │                                      │
  │                                          │ ◀── POST /companies/{id}/devices  │
  │                                          │      { userCode, name, branch, rotation }
  │                                          │ claim: PENDING → CLAIMED, insert device
  │ POST /device-enrollments/{id}/status  │                                      │
  │   Authorization: Bearer C                │                                      │
  │ ◀── { status: "paired", deviceId }       │                                      │
  │ GET /device/self (Bearer C)  ────────▶│ configuration + authorizedUntil       │

The device generates its own credential and sends only its hash when enrollment starts. The credential itself never leaves the device until it is used, the server never returns a secret, and a lost response at any step is retried without issuing anything new. This is the central choice in [ADR-0027](../adr/0027-propose-device-generated-credentials-and-code-based-enrollment.md).

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Enrollment
text:
Enrollment
**Start.** `POST /device-enrollments` is anonymous. The body carries the credential hash (32 bytes, base64url) and the device report (see [capabilities](#capabilities-and-rotation)). The server creates a `PENDING` enrollment valid for 10 minutes and answers with the enrollment ID, the user code, the expiry and a 5-second polling interval. A hash that already belongs to a device or any enrollment is refused with `ENROLLMENT_REJECTED`, so one credential can never bind two identities.
**User code.** Eight characters from the 20-consonant alphabet `BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXZ`, shown as `XXXX-XXXX`, as RFC 8628 section 6.1 recommends: about 34.5 bits, no vowels (no accidental words) and no look-alike digits. Entry ignores case, spaces and hyphens. The server stores an HMAC-SHA-256 of the normalized code under a dedicated `RESTRICTED` key ring (key ID stored with the value, newest key first), never the code, so a database copy does not let anyone enumerate live codes offline. A unique index on the HMAC prevents two live enrollments from sharing a code; a collision on insert is retried with a new code.
**Claim.** In the panel, a person enters the code with a name, a destination branch and a rotation. In one transaction the server locks the company row (tenant data design rule 5), rebuilds the actor's access and requires `devices.manage` on the destination branch and an active company and branch, then moves the enrollment from `PENDING` to `CLAIMED` with a conditional update (`WHERE status = 'PENDING' AND expires_at > now()`), inserts the device with the enrollment's credential hash and report, and writes one `device.paired` audit event. Exactly one of two concurrent claims succeeds; the other, an expired code, a used code and an unknown code all answer the same `PAIRING_CODE_INVALID`, so the answer does not reveal which case applied. The rotation must be one the device reported as supported.
**Status.** The device polls `POST /device-enrollments/{id}/status` with `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`; the server checks the credential against the enrollment's hash. Answers are `pending` (with the polling interval), `paired` (with the device ID) or `expired`. Polling faster than the interval answers `RATE_LIMITED` with the interval to use. Pending enrollments expire lazily: reads treat an expired row as expired and a purge deletes `PENDING` rows one day after expiry, and `CLAIMED` rows 30 days after the claim.
**Commercial hook.** The claim transaction is where PJ-27 will add trial, license and quota admission. Until then only company and branch status gate enrollment.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Device credential and authentication
text:
Device credential and authentication
**Credential.** 32 bytes from the platform CSPRNG, generated and kept by the player in Android Keystore-backed storage (D-07, PJ-12). The server stores only its SHA-256 under a unique index; because the credential has 256 bits of entropy, an unkeyed hash is sufficient for lookup and gives nothing usable from a database copy. The credential is `RESTRICTED`: never in logs, telemetry, errors, audit, query strings or the panel.
**Use.** Device operations declare a new operation access kind, `device`, and expect `Authorization: Bearer <credential>` on paths under `/device/`. The devices module resolves the credential to the device on every request, with no cache, so revocation takes effect on the next request. Device routes never accept the human session cookie, and human routes never accept a device credential. The shared runtime gains only the access kind; the devices module owns the lookup.
**States.** An `ACTIVE` device's credential reaches every device operation. A `REVOKED` device's credential reaches only `GET /device/self`, which answers `{ status: "unlinked", clearRequired: true }`, and `POST /device/self/erasure`, which confirms clearing. Any other credential answers `DEVICE_UNAUTHORIZED` with no detail.
**Rotation.** `POST /device/self/credential` replaces the hash with a new device-generated one. The previous hash stays valid until the new credential is first used, so a lost response leaves the device with a working credential. Rotation is in the last delivery increment; it is not required by the first player.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Check-in and the offline authorization deadline
text:
Check-in and the offline authorization deadline
`GET /device/self` returns the device's ID, name, branch name and time zone, rotation, status and `authorizedUntil`. For an active device, `authorizedUntil` is the database clock plus seven days (AT-15), later capped by a commercial deadline under PJ-27. `PUT /device/self/report` updates the reported capabilities. Each successful device request updates `last_seen_at`, written at most once per minute per device so check-ins do not cause a write per request.
In this design `authorizedUntil` is a server statement in an authenticated HTTPS response. Making it tamper-evident on the device (a signed envelope) and enforcing it against a trusted local clock (AT-16) belong to D-04/PJ-11 and D-07/PJ-12. The panel shows "last seen" and, for unreachable devices, the latest deadline the device could hold, so operators never read server intent as device state.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Capabilities and rotation
text:
Capabilities and rotation
The device report is bounded, validated JSON: application version, protocol version, manufacturer and model (each at most 80 characters), Android version, display width and height in pixels (1 to 16384) and the supported rotations. It is stored as reported and labelled "reported by the device" in the panel; it is not a qualified hardware profile (PH-08), and nothing in this design claims support for a device because it reported a capability.
The configured orientation is a rotation of 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees clockwise: 0 and 180 are horizontal, 90 and 270 vertical (FR-03). A rotation, rather than a horizontal/vertical flag, tells the player which way the screen is physically mounted. Setting a rotation the device did not report as supported answers `ROTATION_UNSUPPORTED`; the panel offers only reported rotations.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Device lifecycle
text:
Device lifecycle
          claim                       unlink                       device confirms clearing
(none) ─────────▶ ACTIVE ───────────────────────────▶ REVOKED, erasure PENDING ───────────▶ REVOKED, erasure CONFIRMED
                  │  rename, set rotation, move           │ record controlled reset (person)
                  │  (same company only)                  └──────────────────────────────▶ REVOKED, erasure RESET_RECORDED

**Rename and rotation.** Need `devices.manage` on the device's branch and the expected version.
**Move.** Changes the branch within the same company. Needs `devices.manage` on both the source and the destination branch, an active destination branch and the expected version. Moving to another company is not an operation: it is an unlink followed by a new enrollment.
**Unlink.** Needs `devices.manage` on the device's branch, the expected version and an explicit confirmation in the panel that names the device. It sets `REVOKED` with erasure `PENDING` in one transaction; from then on the credential reaches only the two operations above. It cannot be undone; the device is paired again with a new enrollment.
**Erasure confirmation.** When an unlinked device reconnects, it learns `clearRequired`, deletes private content, configuration and its credential locally (PJ-12), and only then calls `POST /device/self/erasure` with the credential it is about to discard. The server records `CONFIRMED`, deletes the credential hash and writes `device.erasure_confirmed`. If the response is lost, the device has already cleared and the record stays `PENDING`, shown honestly as unconfirmed, which is the safe direction.
**Controlled reset.** A device that will never reconnect (factory reset, broken, lost) stays `PENDING`. A person with `devices.manage` can record that the device was reset locally; the record says `RESET_RECORDED` with the actor, not `CONFIRMED`, and audit keeps the difference.
**Reassignment.** The server cannot recognize a physical device across identities, so verified cleanup is enforced where it can be: the player starts a new enrollment only from a state with no credential and no private content, and when it still holds a credential it first completes the erasure confirmation above. A new enrollment always creates a new device identity; the old record keeps its own history. The panel lists unlinked devices with their erasure state until the purge below.
Archived branches keep their devices; archiving a branch that still has active devices answers `BRANCH_IN_USE`, through a guard the devices module registers on the organizations access port, so a device is never left in a branch nobody can manage.

heading: Permissions
text:
Permissions
Two capabilities are added to the organizations domain, which owns role presets:
Capability

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Abuse limits
text:
Abuse limits
Proposed initial values:
Enrollment start: the existing per-route rate limit plus at most 20 starts per client address per hour, and at most 10,000 pending enrollments platform-wide, after which starts answer `RATE_LIMITED`. A full pending table makes a guessed code at most 10,000 in 2.56 × 10¹⁰ likely to match.
Claim: at most 10 failed claims per person per 15 minutes and 30 per company per 15 minutes, counted in PostgreSQL from failed-claim rows that record only the actor, company and time. Exceeding a limit answers `RATE_LIMITED` without saying which applied. With these limits an attacker with one account needs on the order of years of attempts per expected match against a full pending table. Many accounts or companies created for guessing remain a residual risk that the signup abuse controls (PH-13) must bound; a successful guess pairs a stranger's screen to the attacker's company, which its owner notices because pairing fails on their side, and no tenant data is exposed.
Status polling: once per polling interval per enrollment.
The per-address limit uses the address Fastify reports for the connection, as the identity routes do; behind a reverse proxy it counts the proxy until trusted forwarding is configured for the production deployment. The general request limit of device routes counts each presented credential instead, under a ceiling of 6,000 requests per address per minute, so screens sharing an address do not exhaust it for each other.
These limits stand on their own; commercial device quotas are PJ-27.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Contracts
text:
Contracts
Human operations (session access, CSRF as elsewhere): `GET /companies/{companyId}/devices` (paginated, cursor-bound, filter by branch and status), `GET .../devices/{deviceId}`, `POST .../devices` (claim), `PATCH .../devices/{deviceId}` (name, rotation, expected version), `POST .../devices/{deviceId}/move`, `POST .../devices/{deviceId}/unlink`, `POST .../devices/{deviceId}/reset-record`. Device operations: the enrollment start and status, `GET /device/self`, `PUT /device/self/report`, `POST /device/self/erasure` and, later, `POST /device/self/credential`. All are TypeBox contracts in the OpenAPI document; the web uses the generated SDK. New expected errors: `PAIRING_CODE_INVALID`, `ENROLLMENT_REJECTED`, `ROTATION_UNSUPPORTED`, `DEVICE_UNAUTHORIZED`, `DEVICE_UNLINKED` (a human change of an unlinked device), `DEVICE_ERASURE_NOT_PENDING` (a reset record without pending erasure), `BRANCH_IN_USE` (organizations), plus the existing `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, `RESOURCE_VERSION_CONFLICT`, `RATE_LIMITED` and strong-authentication errors.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Panel
text:
Panel
A **Screens** view per company (pt-BR "Telas") lists devices with name, branch, status, rotation, last seen and erasure state, filtered to what the person may view. **Pair a screen** asks for the code shown on the TV, a name, a branch the person may manage and a rotation, and shows the reported model and resolution after a successful claim. The device page renames, changes rotation, moves (destinations limited to manageable branches), unlinks with a confirmation naming the device, and records a reset for a pending erasure. Conflicts and unknown outcomes reload and explain, as other company pages do. Copy is in `pt-BR` and `en-US`.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Decisions for review
text:
Decisions for review
The owner approved each item as proposed on 2026-10-19 under [PH-22](human-actions.md#ph-22):
**Enrollment mechanism (ADR-0027).** RFC 8628-style flow owned by the API: the device shows a short code and polls; a signed-in person claims the code in the panel. Devices do not use Keycloak.
**Device-generated credential.** The player generates a 256-bit credential and sends only its SHA-256 at enrollment; the server stores only the hash, never issues a secret and accepts it as a bearer token on device routes only, checked on every request.
**User code.** Eight characters from 20 consonants (`XXXX-XXXX`), valid 10 minutes, single use, stored as a keyed HMAC under a new `RESTRICTED` key ring; every failure answers the same error.
**Abuse limits.** 20 enrollment starts per address per hour, 10,000 pending platform-wide, 10 failed claims per person and 30 per company per 15 minutes, polling once per interval.
**Offline deadline.** Check-in reports `authorizedUntil` as server time plus seven days (AT-15); signing and device-side enforcement are left to PJ-11/PJ-12, and commercial capping to PJ-27.
**Rotation and capabilities.** Rotation of 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees limited to what the device reports; reports are stored as device statements, not qualified support.
**Unlink and reassignment.** Unlink is immediate, irreversible revocation with erasure `PENDING`; the revoked credential can only learn it must clear and confirm clearing; a person may record a controlled reset, shown distinctly from confirmation; another company always pairs a new identity, and the player enrolls only from a cleared state.
**Permissions.** `devices.view` for all roles in their scope; `devices.manage` for administrators company-wide and branch managers on their branches (both branches for a move); operators need a future additional grant.
**Retention (provisional until PH-13).** Unclaimed enrollments deleted one day after expiry, claimed enrollments 30 days after the claim, failed-claim counters after one day; device records and audit are kept with the company; network addresses are never stored.
Approval authorizes implementation of PJ-08 in local and CI environments with simulated players. It does not select hardware (PH-08), implement the Android player (PJ-12) or qualify any physical behavior.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Alternatives considered
text:
Alternatives considered
**Server-issued credential returned once on pairing.** Simpler for the device, but the only copy travels in a response that can be lost, which forces either a re-issue path (more secret-bearing responses) or a stuck device. Rejected in favor of the device-generated credential.
**Device key pair with signed requests (for example DPoP, RFC 9449, or mutual TLS).** Stronger against a copied credential because the private key can stay in Android Keystore hardware, but it adds JWT/proof verification or certificate infrastructure on a single-host pilot with no measured threat requiring it. ADR-0027 keeps the bearer credential behind the `device` access kind so a proof-of-possession scheme can replace it later without changing the enrollment flow.
**Keycloak device grant and service accounts.** Reuses an established implementation, but makes every screen a Keycloak client or user, couples player availability to Keycloak and mixes device and human identities, which the policies keep separate.
**Numeric six-digit codes.** Easier to type on a remote but only about 20 bits; with the same limits an attacker would match a pending code orders of magnitude sooner.
**QR code with a link.** Convenient on phones but puts a credential-bearing link on screen and in browser history; it can be added later as another way to enter the same short code.

title: Teluni Human Actions
heading: Purpose and current state
text:
Purpose and current state
This checklist records Teluni's prerequisites that require a project-owner decision, a human-controlled account action, an unavailable privilege, or securely supplied external configuration. Every contributor or coding agent performing implementation work must maintain it and must never silently skip work because human intervention is needed.
Teluni (https://github.com/GabriellMDias/teluni) was initialized from Orion (https://github.com/GabriellMDias/Orion). Repository settings verified for Orion—Renovate, branch protection, and security controls—do not apply to this repository; the actions below establish them here. Conditional needs such as an identity provider, durable releases, or a deployment environment become new actions when their trigger occurs.

title: Teluni Human Actions
heading: Maintaining this checklist
text:
Maintaining this checklist
Inspect existing decisions, access, tools, configuration, and prior authorization before requesting human intervention. Complete authorized automation and all useful preparation first.
Keep one stable `PH-NN` ID per coherent action; never reuse or renumber IDs. Split broad items into independently verifiable actions as they become concrete, and add newly discovered actions immediately.
Every action retains its ID, checkbox, owner, status, dependency, and evidence. Active or conditional requests also need the exact action, reason, non-secret configuration names, and verification method. Use `pending`, `in progress`, `completed`, `blocked`, or `changed` consistently with the [plan](implementation-plan.md#maintaining-this-plan).
Before asking the user, provide a concrete request: the exact setting or decision, prepared options where appropriate, why automation cannot finish it, affected task IDs, and how completion will be checked.
If an action blocks work now, mark the dependent plan task `blocked`, link this entry, and surface the request to the user. Continue independent authorized work.
Use `[x]` and `completed` only after verification, recording safe evidence and the verification date. If direct verification is unavailable, record the limitation rather than claiming success.
Reopen an action with `[ ]` if later evidence invalidates completion, access expires, or configuration changes, and record why.
A conditional item that becomes unnecessary remains `[ ]` with status `changed`, an explicit reason, and its future trigger or replacement.

title: Teluni Human Actions
heading: Safe configuration handoff
text:
Safe configuration handoff
Record configuration names, required scopes, environment, purpose, non-secret resource identifiers, and secure destination. Never record passwords, tokens, API keys, connection strings containing credentials, private keys, or complete environment dumps here, in the plan, in chat, or in tracked example files.
Name only implemented configuration keys and link the [generated configuration reference](../generated/configuration/api.md); do not invent variable names in advance.
Humans place secrets directly into the selected protected secret store or an explicitly documented ignored local file. Contributors verify presence and authorized behavior without printing secret contents.
Use synthetic local and test data and ephemeral credentials where possible. Production secrets must not be prerequisites for ordinary development or CI.
